solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Contrived return of French artist — about time

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned name goes round the next piece
a return goes back the way it came, so the painter's name is read from the end

parts.note: Edgar Degas, the French painter of ballet dancers

explanation.surface: A dismissive comment that a French painter's comeback was artificial and long overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns DEGAS into SAGED, and 'about' wraps that round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something contrived is artificially arranged, as a scene set up for show is.

clue.text: Cross and unwilling to follow the rules initially

indicators.note: to follow puts the unwilling word after the next letters
initially means taking the first letter of each word

parts.note: averse means unwilling or opposed

explanation.surface: Someone angry and reluctant to obey regulations at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' wants to mean angry; it is the verb. 'initially' takes T and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to traverse is to travel across something.

clue.text: I'm cutting good drug to be worthless

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so these letters go inside the next

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A dealer confessing to diluting good drugs until they're useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' reads as the dealer's diluting of a drug; here it means slicing into.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: gimcrack describes showy but flimsy, cheap things of no real value.

clue.text: Everything I wanted in social flirting

indicators.note: wanted in means wishing to be inside, so these letters go within the next word

parts.note: a social is a party or dance gathering
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone hoping for all they desired at a social event, where flirting happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanted in' is the insertion signal; 'social' is a noun, a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dalliance is casual romantic play, that is flirting.

clue.text: Accommodating chaps after a black filling beer

indicators.note: after places the chaps behind the single letter a in the word being built

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: filling means sitting inside, so the black letter goes into the beer

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A pub scene: obliging fellows topping up a stout or dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' and 'filling' place the pieces; the filled beer makes ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an accommodating person is willing to go along with requests.

clue.text: In reality a missile at end of life mostly has bad performance

parts.note: SAM is a surface-to-air missile

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a term is an end or limit, as a pregnancy comes to term
off means bad, as food goes off
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A grim story of a weapon's last days going badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' takes TERM down to TER; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the phrase means actually or in truth, introducing a fact.

clue.text: What ancient humans used carving up the lion?

indicators.note: carving up means cutting into pieces, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cavemen butchering a lion with whatever was to hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carving up' rearranges THE LION.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a neolith is a polished stone tool of the New Stone Age, used by early people.

clue.text: Beginning to build a foundation for sandstone church

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: silica, quartz, is the main constituent of sandstone

explanation.surface: Builder's advice on laying a base for a sandstone church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beginning to' takes B from build.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a basilica is a large oblong church, often with special papal privileges.

clue.text: Ravel star abandons the piano

indicators.note: abandons means leaves behind, so the letter goes out

parts.note: a pentangle is a five-pointed star
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: A celebrity performer walks away from Ravel's piano music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' looks like the French composer; it is the verb, to tangle. 'abandons' removes P from PENTANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to ravel threads is to twist them into a knotted mess.

clue.text: Our class is left for minutes in West End musical

indicators.note: one letter standing for another means a swap: the minutes letter is replaced

parts.note: Mamma Mia! is the long-running ABBA musical in London's West End theatre district

explanation.surface: A theatregoer notes how the time is spent at a hit show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is left for minutes' means L takes the place of an M; it is the M that begins MIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxonomy: humans belong to the biological class of mammals, whose Latin name this is.

clue.text: Walked about round south-eastern part of England

indicators.note: round means going around, so the reversed word encloses the next letters
about here means turned around, so the past tense of tread is reversed

parts.note: trod is the past tense of tread, to walk

explanation.surface: A rambler's account of hiking about a corner of the English south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives DORT; 'round' wraps it. The county lies in the south-west, so 'south-eastern' is wordplay, not definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Dorset is a county on England's south coast, home of the Jurassic Coast.

clue.text: Female soldier dressed in recycled old and new gear

indicators.note: a soldier dressed in clothes is inside them, so these letters go within the rest
recycled material is broken down and remade, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A woman soldier kitted out in reused uniform, some old and some new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' gives GEORNA; 'dressed in' places the soldier within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Georgina is a woman's given name, so it stands for a female.

clue.text: Very unpleasant pub reported for someone on the fiddle

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: vile means very unpleasant; an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a dodgy bar reported to the authorities for a fraudster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' suggests cheating; here it is literal, a player of the instrument, as in 'second violin' in an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonymy: an orchestra names its players by instrument, so a violin can be a violinist.

clue.text: Memorial is not cheap, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A complaint that a monument's price tag is too high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges NOT CHEAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a cenotaph is a monument to the dead buried elsewhere, like London's Whitehall war memorial.

clue.text: Resistance over chap cutting wages as penny-pinching

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so these letters go inside the next

parts.note: pay means wages

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
Simon is any man's name, standing for a chap

explanation.surface: Workers resist a man slashing their wages, calling it stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' sets resistance first, as this is a down clue; 'cutting' is the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: parsimony is extreme meanness with money.

clue.text: Gesture to attract attention of runner in the countryside

definitions.meaning: a signal with the hand or head summoning someone, as in being at someone's call
a stream, the northern English word for a brook; water runs

explanation.surface: A wave to catch the eye of a cross-country jogger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' suggests an athlete; it is a running stream, the usual word in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a summoning nod or gesture, and a dialect word for a mountain stream.

clue.text: Jane Austen's city quote brought up to ludicrous effect

definitions.note: a noun phrase standing for an adjective: the answer describes what produces that effect

parts.note: Bath, the English spa city where Jane Austen lived

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: A literary quotation from Bath raised for comic effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' makes ETIC, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary sense: bathos is an absurd anticlimax from lofty to trivial, producing a ludicrous effect.

clue.text: Start to remark when tons missed church

indicators.note: missed means left out, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a comment is a remark
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone begins to comment when a heavy load leaves church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' takes T from COMMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to commence is to begin.

clue.text: Learned custom abandoned by university

indicators.note: abandoned by means the following letter leaves, so it is taken out

parts.note: usage means established custom or practice

explanation.surface: An academic custom dropped by a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned by' removes U from USAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sage is wise and learned, as a scholar is.

clue.text: Very good compass and ruler

parts.note: span means range or extent, as does compass
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Praise for a geometry set: a fine pair of compasses and ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compass' and 'ruler' look like drawing instruments; they mean range and monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: spanking means excellent or very fine, as in spanking new.

clue.text: Great European pretentiousness

parts.note: grand means great
EUR is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Seems to be a jibe at a big Continental's airs.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: delusions of grandness are pretension, a show of self-importance.

clue.text: Hearing daughter's embraced by rugby player — sweet

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so these letters go within the next

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby
an ear is the organ of hearing, and having an ear means a good sense of hearing
D is the abbreviation for daughter; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A deaf daughter being hugged by a burly rugby forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' is the insertion. A pear drop is a British boiled sweet with a pear flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the pear drop is a classic pear-flavoured hard candy sold in British sweet shops.

clue.text: Vain person? Love is my middle name

definitions.meaning: a show-off strutting like a bird with a fanned tail
Thomas Love ..., the English satirical novelist and friend of Shelley

explanation.surface: A conceited boast that loving is my defining trait.
explanation.walkthrough: The boast sounds like a vain catchphrase, but read literally it is the novelist Thomas Love Peacock speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a strutting bird used for a show-off, and the writer whose middle name was Love.

clue.text: Book upset many in House of Lords

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the House abbreviation

parts.note: HL is the abbreviation for the House of Lords, Britain's upper chamber

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A book that annoyed many peers in Parliament's upper chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MANY into YMNA, placed 'in' HL.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a hymnal is a church book of hymns, so it is one kind of volume.

clue.text: Pretender's action following ruling to abolish king

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: to abolish means to remove, so the letter goes out

parts.note: reigning means ruling as monarch
R stands for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A political tale of a ruling to scrap the monarchy, prompting a claimant's move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abolish king' leaves EIGNING; R is king from Latin rex.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordplay sense: a pretender is someone who pretends, and the act of pretending is shamming.

clue.text: Working on care for muscle attachment

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the working word comes after

parts.note: to tend is to care for
on means working, as a machine is switched on

explanation.surface: A fitness tip: work on looking after a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is the placing signal: in an across clue the first piece follows the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy: a tendon is the tough fibrous cord joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: Action regularly taken by one who's near spray

indicators.note: taken by places the picked letters before the next piece, which takes them on
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is used

parts.note: near means stingy, so one who's near is a miser

explanation.surface: Seems to describe routine moves by someone standing close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes A, T and O from Action. 'near' is an old word for mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an atomiser turns liquid such as perfume into a fine spray.

clue.text: Leave to investigate the point of paying

definitions.meaning: to depart from a hotel after settling the bill
to look into something to verify it
the till counter in a shop where customers pay

explanation.surface: Seems to be permission to look into where payment happens.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions: the phrasal verb twice, the noun once.
explanation.definitionFit: Three senses: depart from a hotel, look into something, and the counter in a supermarket where you pay.

clue.text: Run back inside tent for food

indicators.note: inside places the reversed letters within the tent word

parts.note: a yurt is a round felt tent of Central Asian nomads

indicators.note: back means going in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to go is to run, as an engine does

explanation.surface: Camping instructions: dash back into the tent for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives OG and 'inside' places it; a yurt is a nomad's felt tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: yogurt is a fermented milk food.
